column1: # doctrine/readme_routes.tsv — the routed-destination registry required by README_POLICY.md
# ("Routing pressure closure"). DATA ONLY: no prose, no derived values, no duplicated counts.
# Moving content out of the README is not enough if the destination becomes an unbounded
# neighbouring sink. Every destination the landing page routes to — as a reader's navigation
# target, or as an author's overflow target named by the guard's own failure hint — has a row
# here with a class, an owner, a pressure control, and where the class demands it, numeric
# ceilings. An unclassified destination is a failed adoption.
# columns:
#   destination        repo-root-relative path (a trailing / means a directory family)
#   route_class        reader_navigation | author_overflow | both
#   lifecycle          hot_live | partitioned | generated_index | append_history | frozen | normative
#   owner              what governs its size and lifecycle
#   health_lines       advisory target: LINES for a file, FILE COUNT for a directory family; 0 = ungoverned
#   health_bytes       advisory target: BYTES for a file, AGGREGATE BYTES for a family; 0 = ungoverned
#   ceiling_lines      enforced ceiling on the same axis as health_lines; 0 = ungoverned
#   ceiling_bytes      enforced ceiling on the same axis as health_bytes; 0 = ungoverned
# A partitioned family's required control is a bounded index PLUS file-count and aggregate
# ceilings — splitting a monolith without bounding the collection moves the same append
# pressure one level down. Family measurements at adoption: docs/tasks/ 5 files / 39,131 B;
# docs/decisions/ 5 / 8,246; docs/knowledge/ 4 / 6,834; docs/book/ 3 / 947;
# docs/provenance/ 5 / 10,860. `docs/` itself stays ungoverned as an umbrella: every family
# inside it carries its own bound, and double-counting would make one row fire for another's
# growth. Its members are the terminals.
# ⛔ Ceilings are DERIVED from this project's own trimmed surfaces, never copied from another
# project. Raising one requires a reviewed decision that the surface's contract expanded.
# Derivation, SEMULITH-PKG.4, measured on the trimmed surfaces:
#   README.md         67 lines / 3,719 B -> health = today, ceiling ~1.27x lines, ~1.31x bytes
#   MEMORY.md         24 lines / 1,380 B -> health ~1.25x; ceiling stays the layer-A contract (50/7168)
#   LIVE_STATUS.md    33 lines / 2,066 B -> health ~1.36x; ceiling ~2.7x (it gains a row per milestone)
#   docs/TASK_TREE.md 52 lines / 2,651 B -> health ~1.25x; ceiling ~2.1x (one row per ACTIVE tree only)
#   CHANGELOG.md     222 lines / 16,228 B -> health 24 KiB; ceiling 64 KiB, then shard
#   DEV_NOTES.md      50 lines /  3,759 B -> health 12 KiB; ceiling 48 KiB, then shard
#   KNOWLEDGE_MAP.md  39 lines /  2,418 B -> derived file; health 8 KiB, ceiling 32 KiB
# A health target set AT today's size fires on the next line and teaches its reader to ignore
# it; these sit a deliberate band below their ceiling instead.
